svg.metadata:
# FigDown — figures as text. Spec: https://github.com/FigDown/figdown
# Reference figure for genre `block` — EXPERIMENTAL constructs ONLY (`CONSTRUCT-STATUS-TIERS`). # Every construct in this file is OUTSIDE the v0.1 conformance surface and # OUTSIDE the compatibility promise: the engine accepts it and renders it # unchanged, but it may change or be withdrawn in a later 0.x WITHOUT a # migration entry. A portable v0.1 block document uses none of it. # The normative surface is block.fd — kept separate so a reader can see # exactly where the promise ends. figdown 0.1 block title "Queue watermarks (experimental constructs)"
# WITHDRAWN — this is where `plane`, its `z-index=` and the `plane=` that # referenced one were demonstrated: three declarations (an implicit 1-based # index, an explicit `z-index=5`, and the empty label that ordered ink and named # nothing), plus a `plane=` on a node, on an `external`, on an edge and on a # bundle. All three writings were WITHDRAWN from the LANGUAGE # (`PAINT-ORDER-CONSTRUCT`) — removed, not renamed, so there is no replacement spelling and no # migration to write: the same shape as the `path`/`routing` withdrawal recorded # in the layout zone at the foot of this file (`EDGE-GEOMETRY-CONSTRUCTS`). The implicit # `base` plane (model z = 0) is unaffected and still there; paint order is # document order. The measurement that carried the withdrawal is in # examples/evpn-fabric.fd: stripping both writings from it and rebuilding # changed EXACTLY ONE of the drawn markup tokens, `data-edge="36"` -> # `data-edge="35"`, and nothing else but the source block the SVG carries and # its hash. The overlay's whole visual identity — `stroke=#dc2626`, dashed — # came from `class=overlay`, which that figure had already declared.
# `stroke=` (border colour) was EXPERIMENTAL until 0.1 and is now # NORMATIVE (`STROKE-KEY-STATUS`); `color=` (label colour) was RETIRED in the same release # (`COLOUR-KEY-STATUS`) and v0.1 has no label-colour key at all — the label colour is derived # from the fill it sits on (core §5, `LABEL-COLOUR-SOURCE`). Nothing on this line is # experimental any more; it is kept because the figure needs the class. class watch "Watched queue" fill=#fef3c7 stroke=#b45309
group pool "Egress queues" stroke=#78716c node q0 "Q0" in=pool class=watch node q1 "Q1" in=pool node q2 "Q2" in=pool node tor "ToR" stroke=#2563eb node sp1 "Spine 1" node sp2 "Spine 2" external core "to the core" # an external takes no option key at all: `plane=` # was its only one (`EXTERNAL-EDGE-ENDPOINTS`/§5) and `PAINT-ORDER-CONSTRUCT` withdrew it
edge q0 -> tor edge q1 -> tor edge q2 -> tor edge tor -- sp1 edge tor -- sp2 edge sp1 -[uplink]-> core stroke=#0f766e # all three labels follow the line (`LABEL-COLOUR-SOURCE`)
flow right rank q0,q1,q2
# WITHDRAWN from this genre — `bundle` was demonstrated here twice: once with a # comma-delimited member list, and once with the empty label of `EMPTY-LABEL-STATE`. It was # WITHDRAWN from `block` (`SCENE-KEYWORD-MEMBERSHIP`). It survives in `topology`, which # can define it BY ITS REFERENT — an IEEE 802.1AX LAG, an ECMP set, an EVPN # Ethernet Segment — where `block`, having no single domain to name one in, had # only the geometric definition "a ring drawn round these links". That is the # per-genre ruling working as designed (`SUBJECT-VOCABULARY-SCOPE`): the same spelling in two genres # was two declarations, and only one of them had a referent to point at. The # member-list form moved to examples/reference/experimental/topology.fd, which # `tools/reference-coverage.js` tracks; the empty-label form did NOT move, so # `bundle` has no `EMPTY-LABEL-STATE` instance in the tree today — `EMPTY-LABEL-STATE` itself is still # demonstrated, in block.fd (`external drop ""`, `group tap ""`).
# EXPERIMENTAL — `threshold`: a marker line across the target at a percentage # of its height (bottom = 0%). No id: nothing references a threshold. The target # is a node or a group; option position is free here too (`OPTION-POSITION-PARSING`). Spelled `guide` # until 0.1 (`THRESHOLD-KEYWORD-SPELLING`) — in every vector editor a "guide" is an author-only # construction line that is never rendered, so the old name was inverted. threshold "80% cap" in=q0 offset=80% stroke=#b91c1c style=dashed threshold in=pool offset=50% "half"
# EXPERIMENTAL — `band`: a NAMED range region. The label is mandatory and # quoted (`BAND-LABEL-STATUS`) and comes first, exactly as on `threshold`; # without it a band asserted nothing a reader could keep, because `fill=` is # presentation and §5 forbids meaning riding on colour alone. The range follows: # `band "X" 60%` is 0..60%; `band "X" 20..40%` is an explicit range in one # token. `..` is the language's ONE range separator (the hyphen form was # retired: between two numbers it reads as subtraction). # `extend=` picks the measuring axis and its 0% edge (`up` = waterline, # `right` = progress bar); it was spelled dir= until 0.1. One band per # axis below so all four values appear — a real figure would share one axis. band "Occupied" 60% in=q0 extend=up fill=#bbf7d0 band "Congested" 20..40% in=q1 extend=down fill=#fecaca stroke=#b91c1c style=dotted band "Drained" 30% in=q2 extend=right fill=#bfdbfe band "Headroom" 15% in=q2 extend=left fill=#e9d5ff # bands stack on one target
# EXPERIMENTAL — a nested `timing` REGION inside this scene document (`GENRE-COMPOSITION`, core # §4). `bitfield`, `table` and `timing` are the three openers with a region # form, and the third is here because the genre itself is experimental: the # composition rule is normative, this instance of it is not. Everything from # here down to `layout` reads under the `timing` genre — `signal` and `gap` are # valid only inside the region, and `node` would be `not valid inside timing`. # The caption is written EMPTY (`EMPTY-LABEL-STATE`): the scene above already says what these # waveforms belong to, and a composed region that repeats its host's words is # the duplication a hybrid figure exists to avoid. timing uplink_up "" fill=#f8fafc signal lacp 0.=.1....... data=pdu stroke=#0ea5e9 signal member 0....1......
layout # The layout zone's whole vocabulary is `pin` (core `LAYOUT-ZONE-NAMESPACE`). It was three until # 0.1: `routing` and `path` were its EXPERIMENTAL half, and this figure # was where they were demonstrated — a `routing orthogonal` line and three # `path` lines showing a per-edge override, a waypoint list with a stored third # coordinate, and the two dock forms. All of it was WITHDRAWN from the language # (`EDGE-GEOMETRY-CONSTRUCTS`; spec/migrations.md 0.1, core §9 `EDGE-IDENTITY-AND-GEOMETRY`), so the reference # figure no longer teaches it — and nothing replaced it, because nothing does # what it did. The edges below draw under auto layout, and this figure scored # BETTER for it on tools/layout-lint.js (4 -> 2): the hand geometry had been # putting the LAG-1 bundle label under a routed stroke — a bundle this figure no # longer draws either, `bundle` having gone the same way in `block` at # 0.3 (`SCENE-KEYWORD-MEMBERSHIP`). Two withdrawals, one file, no migration owed by either. # `pin` is unchanged: `at=` places an element, `width=`/`height=` extend it. pin q0 width=84 height=56 pin q1 width=84 height=56 pin q2 width=84 height=56 pin tor width=84 height=48 pin sp1 at=(350,90) pin sp2 at=(350,170)
